title: `discord.js` support with Deno 1.35
body: I am testing Deno 1.35 on Windows with discord.js 14.11.0, but a basic bot adapted from discordjs.guide fails during client.login() with an AbortError saying "Request aborted". This makes discord.js applications unusable for me despite the announced support, and I saw the problem even before Deno 1.35. My environment is Deno 1.35.0 release for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, V8 11.6.189.7, and TypeScript 5.1.6.

symptoms_visible: On Windows, my basic discord.js bot reaches client.login() and exits with an AbortError saying "Request aborted" instead of becoming ready.
N0.label: N0 discord.js login abort reported

symptoms_visible: I get the abort in native Windows terminals such as PowerShell, CMD, and Git Bash, while the same use under WSL works.
I can also reproduce the same Request aborted stack on a normal Windows 11 Pro installation, not only on a lightweight Windows installation.
N1.label: N1 Windows scope established

symptoms_visible: After updating to Deno 1.35.2, client.login() still ends with "Uncaught AbortError: Request aborted"; the stack includes undici 5.22.1 and a timeout in @discordjs/rest.
N2_x.label: N2_x Deno-only update aftermath

symptoms_visible: With discord.js@dev installed, login still aborts, and the stack still runs through undici rather than completing the request.
N3_x.label: N3_x discord.js dev-tag aftermath

symptoms_visible: My installed dev-tag setup still produces the Request aborted stack during login.
N4.label: N4 dependency evidence collected

symptoms_visible: On my Windows machine with Deno 1.36.1 and discord.js 14.12.1, the client logs in successfully and the Request aborted error is gone.
I still see a message mentioning ClientRequest.options.createConnection, but the login succeeds.
N_terminal.label: terminal login succeeds with stable release

question_patterns: Does this happen in every Windows shell, and does the same program work under WSL?
Can you compare native Windows with a Linux or WSL environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I get it in PowerShell, CMD, and Git Bash on native Windows. The same use works under WSL.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It aborts in WSL and native Windows in exactly the same way.
It fails in PowerShell and CMD but I did not test Git Bash; WSL still works.

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced on a standard Windows installation rather than the lightweight Windows variant?
Could you test the same code on an unaffected-looking stock Windows machine and share the output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it on Windows 11 Pro with Deno 1.35.2. The command still ends in AbortError: Request aborted, with undici and @discordjs/rest paths in the stack.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same code works on stock Windows 11 and only fails on Mini11.
The stock Windows machine uses a different desktop wallpaper and terminal theme.

edges.comment: Thread c0 and c12-c14. The native-Windows versus WSL observation came from participant1; the stock Windows 11 Pro reproduction and stack came from another affected user and were quoted again in c14. Both affected systems are folded into one simulated user side, explicitly ruling out a Mini11-only chain.

solution.intent: Update Deno alone to the next 1.35 patch release on the assumption that the runtime update resolves discord.js login.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to Deno 1.35.2 and rerun the same discord.js client.login() program.

edges.comment: Reporter system from c6: after persistently updating from Deno 1.35.0 to 1.35.2, the same AbortError remained and the pasted stack still passed through undici and @discordjs/rest.

solution.intent: Install the discord.js development tag, expecting it to contain the unreleased Deno compatibility work.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the stable discord.js dependency with discord.js@dev and retry the bot.

edges.comment: Thread c14-c18. The reporter and the affected Windows 11 Pro user both tried the development package and still saw undici in the abort stack. Their outcomes are folded into the reporter side; this was later explained as a dev-tag/dependency publication problem, not evidence that the intended compatibility change itself was ineffective.

question_patterns: Can you paste the exact command and package paths from the failure with the development version?
Which discord.js, @discordjs/rest, and undici paths appear in the dev-tag stack?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran deno run --unstable --allow-all index.ts. The stack names discord.js@14.7.2-dev.1670069017-86959ba.0, @discordjs/rest, and undici@5.22.1 before the request is aborted.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The dev run no longer loads undici; it fails later with an unrelated Discord authentication error.
The same packages appear from the global Deno npm cache rather than a local node_modules directory.

question_patterns: Are newer stable Deno and discord.js releases available now?
Have Deno 1.36 and a new stable discord.js version been released yet?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have seen that Deno 1.36 and a new discord.js release are available, but I do not currently have my devices and asked if someone could check them.

edges.comment: Thread c18 and c24, folding the affected Windows 11 Pro user's raw dev-tag command and stack into the reporter side. The reporter later noted the availability of new stable releases but had not yet performed the successful retest, so no resolution is exposed at this node.

solution.intent: Use a stable discord.js release that includes the runtime-aware REST transport selection, so discord.js uses the runtime's global fetch under Deno instead of the affected undici path; then rerun client.login() on an up-to-date Deno installation.
solution.concrete_example: Update to the stable discord.js release containing the Deno REST compatibility work and retry the bot. The reporter's confirmed working combination was Deno 1.36.1 with discord.js 14.12.1. If ClientRequest.options.createConnection is printed but login succeeds, treat it as a non-fatal compatibility message with a fallback rather than the original abort.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied raw stacks showing that both the stable and dev-tag installations still loaded undici through @discordjs/rest. In c21, the compatibility-change author explained that Deno did not resolve the expected dev tag and that the prerelease pipeline did not point @discordjs/rest at the required dev build. The accepted mechanism is therefore engineer-side inference: a properly released discord.js REST package selects globalThis.fetch on Deno instead of the affected undici request path. The later c29 correction is important—the relevant change was REST via global fetch, not native WebSocket support.

edges.comment: Reporter system from c25: after installing Deno 1.36.1 and discord.js 14.12.1, the reporter confirmed successful login on Windows and declared the issue fixed. Comments c26-c29 explain that the remaining createConnection message is non-fatal and correct the mechanism to REST/global fetch. Comments c31-c32 later confirm discord.js uses globalThis.fetch under Deno and close the original problem as completed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the affected discord.js/@discordjs/rest packages selected undici under Deno, and requests timed out or aborted; this was not specific to the reporter's Mini11 installation.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: undici and @discordjs/rest appear in the Deno 1.35.2 and discord.js development-tag stacks, and the same failure was reproduced on stock Windows 11 Pro while WSL worked.

Must recommend a stable discord.js release containing the runtime-aware REST change that uses globalThis.fetch under Deno, with a current Deno installation, rather than representing a Deno-only patch update as the fix.
Must not recommend discord.js@dev as the resolved path in this case because the tested dev package still resolved dependencies that loaded undici and reproduced the abort.
Must describe the compatibility fix as REST transport selection through global fetch, not as the later native WebSocket support work.

Must ask the user to verify that client.login() succeeds with the stable compatible release before declaring the issue resolved; a remaining ClientRequest.options.createConnection message is not the original failure when login succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Beginner-to-intermediate TypeScript and Discord bot developer. Can adapt sample code, change npm package versions, run Deno commands, and paste stack traces, but asks maintainers to explain package relationships and compatibility messages.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal, concise, and persistent. Shares exact errors and versions, asks direct follow-up questions, and reports successful testing clearly once able to access the Windows machine.
